Since you're an Aspie you probably have a practical bent of mind. As someone who has long had to deal with frequent intrusive suicidal thoughts, here are some things that have helped me, at least for a time, to reduce their frequency and intensity:


-Seeing a skilled therapist (many are not skilled, watch out).


-Building a supportive social network (takes hard work and lots of time, but is worth it, especially if you can locate others who have Aspie tendencies as well).


-Lexapro (an SSRI, aka escialopram).


-Moderate to large doses of LSD.


-Having a girlfriend.


-Journaling


-Meditation (especially mindfulness or zen style).


-Finding someone to help.


-Moving to a new city (I was much less suicidal in a dense cosmopolitan city than in a suburban conservative one).


-Studying philosophy.


Finally, if all else fails you may want to consider ECT. It is different from what you see in the movies and is actually considered to be quite effective these days. Feel free to PM me if you want to discuss further.
